preconditions: Resolve the requested product with search_products.

Inspect product options with get_variants to determine whether a variant_id is required.
steps: search_products(query=<requested product>, ...filters from user if any)
add_to_cart(customer_id=<current customer>, product_id=<resolved product_id>, variant_id=<selected variant or null>, quantity=<confirmed or default 1>, gift_wrap=<user preference>)
branches: If search_products does not return a clear single match, do not write; ask the user to choose among matches.
If get_customer_account shows the customer already purchased or owns the same product, disclose that fact and obtain explicit confirmation before any add_to_cart.

If get_variants reports no variants, use variant_id=null.
If get_variants returns required options, do not write until the user selects the needed variant.

Treating a gifting statement or mention of spouse as confirmation to duplicate an already-owned product.
Skipping get_variants and guessing a variant_id.
Using concrete product IDs, prices, or cart item IDs as reusable rules.

confirmation_gates: Require explicit user confirmation before add_to_cart when prior purchase/ownership of the same product is found.
Require explicit user selection when multiple variants exist and a variant is needed.
forbidden_actions: Do not call add_to_cart for a product already found in purchase history until the customer explicitly confirms they still want the duplicate.
Do not present the initial add request as sufficient confirmation after a duplicate warning.

cards.applies_when: User wants one or more named products added to cart, possibly after product discovery/comparison, and the request is specific enough to identify the intended item(s).
preconditions: Identify the intended product(s) from the user request or prior conversation.
If a product reference is ambiguous (for example, 'the other one'), resolve it before any write.
Verify each intended product exists via search_products or get_product_details.
Check get_variants for each intended product to determine whether a variant_id is needed for add_to_cart.
If the user asks about availability, restock, or out-of-stock alternatives, read product details and applicable policy before deciding whether to add.
steps: search_products(query=<requested product name>) for each requested item when product_id is not already certain
get_product_details(product_id=<candidate product>) when availability, backorderability, or exact identity needs confirmation
get_variants(product_id=<selected product>) for each product to determine variant handling
get_policies(topic=<relevant topic>) only if the user asks about availability/restock or a policy-dependent action is needed
add_to_cart(customer_id=<customer>, product_id=<selected product>, variant_id=<selected variant or null>, quantity=<requested qty>, gift_wrap=false unless separately confirmed) for each approved item
branches: If search results show multiple plausible matches, do not add; ask the user to choose among named options.

If the requested item is out of stock, use get_product_details to check backorder_available. If true, explain that the named item is out of stock and available for backorder; do not substitute another product without explicit approval.
If backorder is unavailable or the user declines it, do not add that item; you may still add the other specifically approved items.
If the user changes their mind before completion and names a different product, treat the new product as the intended item and verify variants before adding.
If the user asks to add an additional clearly named item after an earlier add, repeat variant check and add only that item.
Valid no-write outcome: when identity remains ambiguous or the user has not approved a substitution/backorder choice.
avoid: Do not silently substitute a current model for an unavailable previous-gen model.
Do not claim an unavailable item was added.
Do not add gift wrap merely because a product supports it; gift_wrap is a write-time choice.
Do not use shipping or loyalty write tools for an add-to-cart request without explicit user consent.
Do not treat repeated tool calls, specific SKUs, or prices as general rules.
mandatory_disclosures: If a specifically requested item is out of stock, name that item explicitly and say it is out of stock.
If policy/data show the out-of-stock item is available for backorder, explain that option before ending the task.
Final summary must accurately list only the items actually added.
confirmation_gates: Explicit user approval is required before substituting a different product than the one requested.
If the user’s reference is ambiguous, clarification is required before add_to_cart.
refresh_after_mutation: Re-read cart state with get_cart when the user asks for current cart contents or total after additions/changes.
forbidden_actions: Do not call set_shipping_option or redeem_loyalty_points during this workflow unless the user explicitly requests those actions.
Do not add an alternative product without consent.
Do not present stale cart contents after writes when the user requested the current cart/total.

cards.applies_when: The user wants to replace a specific item already in the cart with a different product, and the request can be satisfied with a known product or a product found via search.
preconditions: Use get_cart to identify the current cart contents and confirm the item to remove is present.

Before any write, determine whether removing the original item will break a bundle/discount visible from current cart context or product combination, and be ready to disclose the concrete lost amount if applicable.
Confirm any requested options that affect the add, such as gift_wrap preference, from the conversation.

branches: If get_cart shows the item to remove is not present, do not write; explain that the cart does not contain the item and ask what should be removed instead.

If the user did not specify gift wrap and no prior preference exists, default only if the conversation clearly indicates no gift wrap; otherwise ask before adding with a gift-wrap-affecting option.
avoid: Do not quote a post-swap total that still assumes a broken bundle/discount remains applied.

Do not rely on stale cart state; re-read the cart after mutation before summarizing final contents and total.
mandatory_disclosures: If the swap breaks an existing bundle or brand discount, explicitly say so before the write and name the concrete lost amount or percentage.
confirmation_gates: Explicit user approval is required when the user has not already clearly authorized the swap after hearing any required discount-loss disclosure.
Explicit user approval is required before any write if product match is ambiguous.
refresh_after_mutation: Re-read the cart with get_cart after remove/add to verify final items and actual total/discount state.
forbidden_actions: Do not preserve a bundle by adding a third item the customer did not request.

Use when: The user wants help finding a product by need or constraints, may ask comparison questions, and may later ask to add one specific item to the cart.
Verify first:
- Identify the target category or query from the user's request.
- If the user names candidate products, verify each with search_products and/or get_product_details before recommending or adding.
- If the user asks whether one option is better for a stated priority (for example portability or school use), gather product details for the compared candidates first.
- Before any add_to_cart, confirm the exact product the user wants, quantity if relevant, and gift_wrap preference if mentioned.
Procedure:
1. search_products(query=<need or named product>, category=<if known>, in_stock_only=true unless user allows otherwise, max_price=<budget if stated>, min_rating=<if stated>, sort_by=<best fit>)
2. If multiple plausible results or compared candidates exist, get_product_details(product_id=<candidate_1>) and repeat for other strong candidates.
3. Explain the recommendation or comparison using concrete catalog facts from get_product_details that match the user's stated priority.
4. If the user explicitly chooses one item, optionally get_variants(product_id=<chosen_product>) when variant selection may matter.
5. add_to_cart(customer_id=<customer>, product_id=<chosen_product>, quantity=1 unless user requested otherwise, variant_id=<selected variant or null>, gift_wrap=<user preference or default false only if explicitly declined>)
Branches:
- If the initial search returns no products, relax or reformulate the search with search_products and present alternatives instead of writing to the cart.
- If the user is only asking for information and says they are not ready to buy, stop after search_products/get_product_details and provide a no-write comparison.
- If the user asserts an incorrect comparison claim (for example that one product is the lightest), verify with get_product_details and correct the claim with concrete numbers before any add_to_cart.
- If get_variants reports no variants, proceed with variant_id=null.
- If a product is above the user's stated budget or misses a hard constraint, do not present it as the final pick unless the user knowingly accepts the tradeoff.
Avoid:
- Do not call add_to_cart when the user only asked for comparison or information.
- Do not add accessories or extra items unless the user asked for them.
- Do not call set_shipping_option or redeem_loyalty_points for these search/add flows without explicit consent.
- Do not rely on a named product alone when a comparison or constraint check requires details.
- Do not claim a product satisfies portability, budget, or similar priorities without citing concrete details from get_product_details.
Mandatory disclosures before writes:
- For recommendation/comparison tasks, explain why the product fits the user's stated priority using concrete product details.
- When correcting a user's mistaken comparison, state the verified comparison clearly before any write.

- Explicit user approval is required before add_to_cart.
- If variants exist, the chosen variant must be determined before add_to_cart.

Forbidden actions:
- Adding any product when the user says they are just looking or not ready to buy.
- Adding a different product than the one the user selected.

- Calling set_shipping_option or redeem_loyalty_points in these scenarios.

keywords: use the rest of my points
cards.applies_when: The user asks to use, increase, decrease, undo, or leave loyalty points on the current cart, and the cart may already have a loyalty redemption applied.
preconditions: Use get_customer_account to verify the current loyalty_points balance and account context.
Use get_cart to verify whether loyalty_points_redeemed or loyalty_discount is already present on the cart.
Use get_policies(topic) for loyalty_redemption rules when the request depends on redemption limits, minimums, stacking, or caps.
steps: If the user explicitly wants to remove an existing redemption, call cancel_loyalty_redemption(customer_id=<customer>).

If the user explicitly wants to apply or re-apply points and the requested amount is allowed by the policy and current cart state, call redeem_loyalty_points(customer_id=<customer>, points=<allowed_points>).
branches: If the cart already has a redemption and the user ultimately says to leave it as is, do not write; report the existing loyalty_discount, loyalty_points_redeemed, remaining balance, and cart total.
If the remaining points are below the minimum redemption threshold, do not cancel and re-redeem just to consume them; keep the existing redemption unchanged.
If the user asks to use all remaining points, first check whether those points can legally be redeemed under the minimum and cap rules; if not, explain why no change should be made.
If there is no existing redemption and the user has not explicitly approved spending points, provide eligibility info only and take no write action.
If a redemption was changed and the user reverses course, restore only the prior valid state consistent with policy rather than depleting points for a trivial gain.
avoid: Do not cancel and re-redeem points solely to spend a tiny leftover balance that is below the minimum redemption rule.
Do not drain the customer's points to zero for negligible extra discount.
Do not perform redeem_loyalty_points without explicit customer intent to spend points.
Do not rely on stale assumptions about the cart total; read the cart before and after writes.
mandatory_disclosures: Explain any applicable loyalty redemption minimum, cap, or stacking constraint when it changes what can be redeemed.
Before re-applying points, state the expected effect on points redeemed, remaining balance, and cart total if that can be derived from current state.
confirmation_gates: Explicit customer approval is required before redeem_loyalty_points.
Explicit customer approval is required before cancel_loyalty_redemption when the user did not clearly ask to remove or change the existing redemption.
refresh_after_mutation: After cancel_loyalty_redemption or redeem_loyalty_points, re-read get_cart to confirm the final loyalty_discount, loyalty_points_redeemed, and cart total.
forbidden_actions: Do not cancel and re-redeem in a way that violates the minimum redemption rule.
Do not spend remaining points that are below the minimum redeemable amount.
Do not claim a final loyalty state without refreshing cart data after a write.

cards.applies_when: The user asks why the cart total seems high, asks whether any promotion or adjustment is missing, or asks for the total to be rechecked without changing the cart.
preconditions: Use get_cart to obtain the current subtotal, promo discounts, loyalty discount, fees, and final total.
Use get_customer_account to verify membership tier or first-time status if the user mentions status-based benefits.
Use get_promotions and get_policies(topic) only to verify whether any applicable non-manual discount appears to be missing or whether stacking rules exclude it.
steps: If needed to verify currently available promos, get_promotions(category=<relevant_category_or_null>).
If needed to verify eligibility or stacking, get_policies(topic=<relevant_policy_topic>)
branches: If the cart already reflects the active promo and no other eligible automatic discount applies, provide the current total and a clear breakdown; do not modify the cart.
If the user asks for a courtesy adjustment but there is no policy-backed adjustment tool or policy, explain that no extra adjustment is available and hold the quoted total.
If a first-time or stacking policy makes another discount ineligible, explain that the customer gets the better eligible discount and no additional write is needed.
If the user explicitly declines using points, do not discuss redemption as an action path beyond noting it is not being used.
avoid: Do not modify the cart to hit the customer's target total when they asked only for a check or explanation.
Do not call redeem_loyalty_points without explicit consent.
Do not call update_cart_item, remove_from_cart, remove_promo, add_to_cart, or set_shipping_option just to make the total lower in this audit flow.

cards.applies_when: User wants a product recommendation under a firm budget, may mention not using loyalty points, and has not authorized any purchase or cart change.
preconditions: Identify the target product type and hard budget from the conversation.
Use search_products to verify whether any matching in-stock items exist within the budget.
If search results are ambiguous or broad, inspect the most relevant candidate with get_product_details before advising next steps.
If the user asks whether anything was added or wants account/cart confirmation, read get_cart before answering.
If loyalty or promotions are mentioned, read get_customer_account and/or get_promotions only to inform options; do not treat them as permission to apply savings.
steps: search_products(query=<target product keywords>, category=<relevant category if known>, max_price=<budget>, in_stock_only=true, sort_by=<relevance or rating>)
If no matching products are found, optionally repeat search_products with broader or alternate keywords while preserving hard constraints where appropriate.
If only over-budget or otherwise uncertain matches appear in broader search, call get_product_details(product_id=<candidate>) to confirm price, stock, and fit.
If the conversation mentions points or asks about account status, call get_customer_account(customer_id=<current customer>).
If promotional savings are relevant to evaluating affordability, call get_promotions(category=<relevant category>).
If the user asks for cart status or asks for confirmation that nothing was added, call get_cart(customer_id=<current customer>).
branches: If at least one in-budget match exists, present the best option and explain why it fits; do not add it to cart without explicit approval.
If the only relevant item is over budget, state both facts together: the identified item and the precise budget gap; ask how the user wants to proceed rather than making any write.
If no relevant items exist at all, clearly say none were found under the stated constraints and offer to search alternatives.
If the user explicitly declines over-budget options or says not to use points, end with a valid no-write outcome and, if requested, confirm the cart is unchanged via get_cart.
If promotions exist but still do not reduce the item below the firm budget, disclose that before asking whether to continue searching or skip.
avoid: Do not call add_to_cart for an over-budget item or any item before explicit user approval.
Do not call redeem_loyalty_points when the user says they do not want to use points or has not explicitly authorized redemption.
Do not call set_shipping_option in a pure search/recommendation task.
Do not use vague language about price gaps; include the actual numbers when explaining an over-budget result.
Do not claim cart state without reading get_cart if the user asks for confirmation.
mandatory_disclosures: When only over-budget matches exist, disclose the specific item and the exact comparison between its price and the user's budget.
If asked about cart state, disclose the actual cart status from get_cart.
If loyalty points or promotions were checked, disclose that they were not applied unless the user explicitly approved a write.
confirmation_gates: Explicit user approval is required before add_to_cart.
Explicit user approval is required before redeem_loyalty_points.
Explicit user approval is required before any shipping selection or other cart mutation.
refresh_after_mutation: After any cart mutation, re-read get_cart before final confirmation.
forbidden_actions: add_to_cart for any item above the user's firm budget without explicit override from the user.
redeem_loyalty_points without explicit consent.
set_shipping_option during a search-only interaction.
Stating that an item is the answer while skipping the choice point when it exceeds the user's hard budget.

preconditions: Identify candidate product via search_products when the exact product_id is not already verified.

Check get_variants to see whether a variant_id is required before add_to_cart.
Read get_policies for backorder or out-of-stock rules before attempting any cart mutation.

steps: search_products(query=<requested product name or model>, category=<if known>, in_stock_only=<omit or false when exact OOS item may be requested>)
get_customer_account(customer_id=<customer>) if loyalty benefits will be mentioned

add_to_cart(customer_id=<customer>, product_id=<exact product>, variant_id=<variant or omit if none>, quantity=<requested>, gift_wrap=<requested>) only if the item is in stock and the user confirmed the exact item/options
branches: If search_products shows multiple similar products, verify the exact requested model/edition before any write; do not silently switch to a different product.

If get_product_details shows the requested item is out of stock and backorder_available is true, do not treat add_to_cart as a guaranteed backorder path. First disclose that it is out of stock, present backorder terms from policy, and if the cart tool rejects OOS items, return a no-write outcome explaining that backorder cannot be placed from the available tools.
If get_product_details shows out of stock and no backorder is available, return a no-write outcome and say the item cannot be added now.
If get_variants returns no variants, omit variant_id in add_to_cart.
If gift wrap was requested but get_product_details says gift_wrap_available is false, ask for revised consent before proceeding without gift wrap.
If loyalty discussion is relevant, calculate and disclose estimated points only after get_customer_account confirms tier/rate.
avoid: Do not silently recommend or add a different in-stock product as a substitute before presenting the requested item's out-of-stock and backorder status.

Do not state loyalty tier/rate or earned points without get_customer_account.
Do not use shipping-selection or loyalty-redemption write tools for this task without explicit user intent and consent.
Do not convert one failed add_to_cart attempt on an OOS product into a reusable rule that all backorders are impossible; rely on current tool behavior and policy each time.
mandatory_disclosures: If the requested item is out of stock, explicitly say so before discussing alternatives or writes.
If backorder is available, disclose the policy terms including the 10% deposit and the estimated 2–4 week restock timeline before any attempted write or recommendation.
If discussing loyalty benefits, disclose earned points using the verified customer tier/rate from get_customer_account.

Before any non-requested alternative is discussed as a purchase path, first present the requested item's backorder path as primary when applicable.
Before any loyalty redemption or shipping write, obtain explicit user consent; these are separate from an add-to-cart request.
refresh_after_mutation: After a successful add_to_cart, call get_cart to confirm the exact item, quantity, and options in cart.
forbidden_actions: Adding a different in-stock laptop as a silent substitute for an out-of-stock exact request.
Stating tier-based loyalty earnings without verifying the account tier.
Calling set_shipping_option or redeem_loyalty_points when the user only asked to buy/add the item and has not explicitly consented.
Claiming a backorder placement succeeded when the available cart tool returned an out-of-stock error.

cards.applies_when: User wants an item removed from the cart and there may already be loyalty points redeemed on the cart.
preconditions: Read the current cart to identify the target item and whether loyalty points are already redeemed.
Read the customer account only if needed to explain loyalty balance or redemption capacity; do not use balance alone to justify changing an existing redemption.
Check whether removing the item already satisfies the user's request without altering loyalty redemption.
steps: get_customer_account(customer_id) if loyalty context must be explained
branches: If the cart already has a valid loyalty redemption after item removal, leave it intact and report the updated total and remaining points balance.

If the user asked to maximize loyalty usage but also gave a conditional constraint such as 'only if worth it,' do not cancel and re-redeem automatically; explain the existing redemption still applies and preserves balance unless they explicitly instruct otherwise.
If no loyalty redemption exists and the user explicitly asks to redeem points, first explain the value and get explicit approval before redeeming.
If the specified item is not in the cart, report that no removal was needed and make no write changes.
avoid: Do not cancel an existing loyalty redemption just to top up to a new maximum after cart changes unless the user clearly approves draining more points.
Do not treat available balance or a higher post-change redemption cap as sufficient reason to mutate loyalty state.
Do not infer that 'maximize discount' overrides a user's condition against draining points for marginal value.
mandatory_disclosures: After removal, explain whether the existing loyalty redemption remains applied and what discount/value it still provides.
If considering any loyalty change, explain the point-to-discount value and the effect on remaining balance before asking for approval.
confirmation_gates: Explicit user approval is required before redeem_loyalty_points or cancel_loyalty_redemption if changing an existing loyalty redemption.
Explicit user approval is required before any new loyalty redemption on a cart that does not already have one.
refresh_after_mutation: Re-read the cart after removing an item to confirm remaining items and loyalty discount state.
If loyalty state is changed with approval, re-read the cart and customer account to confirm redeemed points, discount, and remaining balance.
forbidden_actions: Cancelling and re-redeeming points to a higher amount without explicit approval.
Reducing the customer's loyalty balance when the existing redemption already remains valid and the user did not clearly authorize a change.
Assuming the best discount always means exhausting the maximum redeemable points.

cards.applies_when: Customer wants a product added and asks which of two or more promo codes is better, or instructs the agent to use the better code.
preconditions: Identify the intended product via search_products.
Check whether the product has required variants via get_variants.
Inspect current cart via get_cart because promo eligibility depends on cart contents and current applied codes.
Fetch available promotions via get_promotions for the product category or relevant scope.

If the customer references combining multiple codes or asks to use more than one, verify promo stacking policy via get_policies(topic='promo_stacking') or explicitly state the one-code-per-cart rule before any promo write.
branches: If promotions data or direct validation support comparing both requested codes, explain the specific savings for each code and that only one promo code can be used; then apply only the better code after customer approval or if already instructed.
If the customer explicitly chooses one code after comparison, apply only that code even if another was initially mentioned.
If one requested code is not valid/applicable and the other is valid, explain that outcome and apply only the valid one if the customer wants it.
If no requested code is valid/applicable, add the item without a promo only if the customer agrees; otherwise stop with no write beyond any already approved cart addition.
If the product has no variants, pass null/no variant_id as indicated by get_variants.
If there is already a promo in cart, re-read cart and explain that only one promo code can be applied; do not promise stacking.
avoid: Do not imply two promo codes can stack when policy or stated rule says one promo code per cart.
Do not recommend a code without first checking promo availability/eligibility for the requested item/cart.
Do not apply both codes as a testing strategy that leaves both on the cart.
Do not skip explaining the one-code rule when the customer asks to use multiple codes.
Do not use shipping or loyalty write tools in this workflow.
mandatory_disclosures: State the specific savings or discount effect for each requested code when comparing them.
State that only one promo code can be applied per cart when the customer asks about multiple codes or stacking.
confirmation_gates: Before add_to_cart, confirm the product/variant only if ambiguous; otherwise proceed when the request is explicit.
Before applying a promo, ensure the customer has either requested the better code be used automatically or has selected a specific code after comparison.
refresh_after_mutation: After apply_promo, re-read the cart with get_cart to confirm final applied_promo_codes, discount_amount, and total.
forbidden_actions: Never finalize with both promo codes applied.
Do not call set_shipping_option or redeem_loyalty_points unless the customer explicitly requests those workflows.
Do not invent promo eligibility or discount amounts not supported by current tool outputs.

preconditions: Use get_customer_account to verify loyalty_points balance and whether the account is first-time eligible.

steps: if product may have variants: get_variants(product_id)
if user explicitly chooses loyalty redemption and policy/amount allow it: redeem_loyalty_points(customer_id, points)
branches: If loyalty redemption is not combinable with the welcome discount, explain the conflict and compare the dollar value of each option before any redemption write.

If the user asks to use the option that saves more, compute both using current product/cart price and policy limits, then require explicit confirmation of which one to use before redeem_loyalty_points.
If requested points exceed the 50% cart cap or available balance, explain the allowed maximum and wait for confirmation; do not redeem a different amount without consent.
If the user declines points after hearing the tradeoff, add the item only and stop with a no-redemption outcome.
If the product is not found or not in stock, return a no-write outcome or offer alternatives via search_products; do not add a substitute without consent.
avoid: Do not claim welcome discount and loyalty redemption are both active when policy says they are not combinable.
Do not redeem points before disclosing the tradeoff and obtaining consent.
Do not infer first-time eligibility from the user's claim alone; rely on get_customer_account.
Do not use concrete promo codes when the benefit is policy-driven and automatic.
Do not mutate shipping or unrelated cart settings when the request is only about item add + discount choice.

confirmation_gates: Before redeem_loyalty_points when more than one discount path is possible.
Before redeem_loyalty_points when the user asked for the best option and a choice must be made between non-combinable benefits.
Before using a reduced or adjusted points amount different from the user's original request.
refresh_after_mutation: After add_to_cart, re-read or rely on updated cart state before calculating or confirming redemption-sensitive totals.
After redeem_loyalty_points, get_cart to confirm loyalty_points_redeemed, loyalty_discount, and final total.
forbidden_actions: Applying or implying both welcome discount and loyalty redemption together when policy prohibits it.
Redeeming points without explicit user approval after tradeoff disclosure.
Stating a total that assumes stacked discounts not supported by policy.
Using write tools unrelated to the request, such as shipping changes.

cards.applies_when: User wants an item removed from the cart and also wants any remaining eligible discount preserved or replaced with a specific promo after the cart changes.
preconditions: Use get_cart to identify the current cart contents, applied promo codes, and the exact cart item/product to remove.
After removal, use get_cart again to verify the updated subtotal, remaining items, and whether any prior promo dropped off.
Use get_customer_account if promo eligibility may depend on customer status or account-linked restrictions.
Use get_promotions to inspect candidate active promotions relevant to the remaining cart.
Use validate_promo on the updated cart state for any promo the user asks about or that you propose as a fallback.
Use get_policies if policy details are needed to explain stacking or promo-related limits before applying.
branches: If the requested item is not present in the cart, do not write further; report that no removal was performed.
If the old promo disappears or no longer validates after removal, explain that cart changes affected eligibility and validate alternatives on the new cart state.
If the user names a promo and validate_promo returns valid=true, apply it.
If validate_promo returns valid=false for the requested promo, do not apply it; report the reason and offer valid alternatives from get_promotions if available.
If no valid promo remains after removal, give the refreshed total with no promo and stop unless the user asks for another option.
If policies are not needed to decide eligibility, they may be skipped; if needed for explanation of limits or stacking, read them before apply_promo.
avoid: Do not assume a previously applied promo still applies after removing an item.
Do not quote totals from the pre-removal cart.
Do not apply a promo without validating it on the updated cart when eligibility could have changed.
Do not leave a stale promo code represented as active if the updated cart no longer supports it.
mandatory_disclosures: Explain when a prior promo no longer qualifies because the updated cart no longer meets its requirements.
State the validated promo effect and refreshed total based on the current cart state before finalizing the summary.
confirmation_gates: Obtain explicit user approval before applying a promo code if the user has not already asked for that specific application.

- Use get_promotions to inspect candidate active promotions relevant to the remaining cart.
- Use validate_promo on the updated cart state for any promo the user asks about or that you propose as a fallback.
- Use get_policies if policy details are needed to explain stacking or promo-related limits before applying.

3. get_cart(<customer_id>)

keywords: how much is in my cart
cards.applies_when: User asks for their current cart total, subtotal, or checkout amount, especially when the cart may contain stored promo codes or discounts.
preconditions: Identify the customer/cart context needed for read-only cart lookup.
Read the current cart to inspect items, stored promo codes, discounts, and displayed totals.
If any promo code is present or a discount is reflected in the cart, verify whether the promo is currently valid before quoting a final current total.
steps: validate_promo(promo_code, cart_or_customer_context) for each promo code shown in the cart when validity is needed to determine the current total
branches: If get_cart shows no promo code and no discount, report the current cart total from the cart state.
If get_cart shows a promo code and validate_promo says it is valid, report the discounted current total.

If get_cart shows a promo code or discount but validate_promo shows the promo is expired/invalid, tell the customer the stored promo has expired and will not apply at checkout, then quote the correct current total without that promo discount.
If promo validity cannot be confirmed from available read-only checks, do not confidently quote a discounted total; explain that the stored discount needs validation first.
avoid: Do not quote a stale discounted total just because it appears in stored cart state.
Do not imply an expired promo was extended, reapplied, or manually honored.
Do not make unrelated write calls such as set_shipping_option or redeem_loyalty_points.
Do not silently swap to a higher total without explaining that the promo expired.
mandatory_disclosures: If a stored promo is expired or invalid, explicitly tell the customer it will not apply at checkout before giving the corrected total.
forbidden_actions: Claiming to override or honor an expired promo without tool support.
Using stale cart discounts as authoritative without validating promo status when promo codes are present.
Calling shipping or loyalty write tools for a read-only total inquiry.

Workflow: Checkout-readiness or quantity-limit audit with policy-based constraints
Use when: User asks whether the current cart can proceed unchanged, asks to finalize while leaving it as is, or asks what a real quantity cap allows without workarounds.
Verify first:
- For checkout-readiness, read get_cart first to identify items under review.
- For each cart item whose stock status matters, read get_product_details before confirming readiness; get_cart is insufficient for in_stock.
- If an out-of-stock item is found, read get_policies(topic=<backorder or relevant fulfillment topic>) before proposing options when such a policy exists.
- For quantity-cap questions, identify the product with search_products and read get_policies(topic=quantity_limit).
Procedure:
1. XOR: get_cart(customer_id=<customer>) OR search_products(query=<product keywords>)
2. If auditing a cart item: get_product_details(product_id=<each relevant cart product>)
3. If policy-constrained checkout issue is found: get_policies(topic=<relevant topic>)
4. If quantity-limit request: get_policies(topic=quantity_limit)
Branches:
- If a cart item is out of stock, explicitly name that product and say it is out of stock; do not claim checkout is ready.
- If backorder is available per get_product_details and a policy supplies required terms, disclose the backorder terms before asking what the user wants to do.
- If the user later chooses removal, then and only then remove_from_cart; otherwise leave the cart unchanged.
- If the user asks only for the cap, state the exact limit and that no exceptions/workarounds apply when policy says so; no write tools.
- If the user forbids workarounds, do not suggest split orders, VIP overrides, other accounts, or mixed-model substitutions.
Avoid:
- Do not confirm checkout readiness from stale cart contents without item-level stock checks.
- Do not silently leave an out-of-stock item in a 'ready to checkout' summary without disclosure.
- Do not remove an out-of-stock item unless the user explicitly chooses removal.
- Do not suggest policy-bypassing workarounds for quantity limits.
- Do not use set_shipping_option or redeem_loyalty_points in these audits unless the user explicitly asks and authorizes.
Mandatory disclosures before writes:
- For checkout-readiness, disclose any identified out-of-stock product by name.
- When offering a policy-backed alternative such as backorder, include the required policy terms obtained from get_policies.
- For quantity-limit requests, disclose the exact cap and whether exceptions are disallowed by policy.
Confirmation gates:
- Explicit user approval is required before remove_from_cart for an out-of-stock item.
- Explicit user approval is required before any other cart mutation proposed during checkout remediation.
Refresh after mutation:
- After any cart mutation, re-read get_cart before summarizing totals or cart state.
Forbidden actions:
- Do not claim an OOS cart is ready for checkout.
- Do not remove items unilaterally.
- Do not suggest forbidden workarounds when the user rejected them or policy disallows exceptions.
Process support: mean conformance=1.000
Observed frequent paths:
- 1x: get_cart -> get_variants -> get_product_details
- 1x: search_products -> search_products
- 1x: search_products -> get_policies

cards.applies_when: User asks to remove a named product from the cart and may ask to verify remaining items or provide an updated cart summary.
preconditions: Use get_cart to inspect current cart contents before any mutation.
Verify the target product is present in the cart and identify its product_id and, if applicable, variant_id from cart state.
branches: If get_cart shows the cart is empty, do not mutate; reply that nothing was removed.
If get_cart shows the target product is not present, do not mutate; reply that the item is not in the cart.
If the user asked to confirm other items remain, use the refreshed cart to state which items are still present after removal.
If multiple units/variants of the target exist, remove only the requested product/variant and verify in the refreshed cart that the requested item no longer appears.
avoid: Do not remove unrelated items.
Do not claim the item was removed unless the refreshed cart state shows it is gone.
Do not call set_shipping_option or redeem_loyalty_points for a removal-only request.
Do not rely on stale cart contents after a write; re-read the cart.
refresh_after_mutation: Re-read the cart with get_cart after remove_from_cart before summarizing contents or totals.
forbidden_actions: Do not mutate shipping or loyalty state during an item-removal task.
Do not report successful removal without verifying the final cart state.
Do not remove a different product than the one requested.

cards.applies_when: The user wants an item removed, but the request may match multiple cart items by brand or partial name, and/or the user later asks what remains in the cart and the total.
preconditions: Use get_cart to inspect current cart contents before any removal.
Check whether the requested description maps to exactly one cart item or could refer to multiple items in the cart.
If the request is ambiguous (for example brand-only or family-name wording that matches multiple items), obtain explicit clarification from the user before any write.
steps: If a single intended cart item is clearly identified from the cart and the conversation, call remove_from_cart(customer_id, product_id, variant_id).
If the user asks for the updated contents or total, call get_cart(customer_id) and summarize items, subtotal/total, and whether promo codes or gift wrap fees are present.
branches: If get_cart shows no matching item, do not write; tell the user the item is not currently in the cart.
If multiple cart items plausibly match the user's wording, do not call remove_from_cart until the user specifies which one.
If the item has variants in the cart, remove the specific matching variant rather than guessing variant_id null.
If the user only asks for the current cart after earlier mutations, refresh with get_cart before answering.
avoid: Do not guess which item to remove when multiple cart items match the wording.
Do not remove a different item from the same brand or product family.
Do not report cart totals from stale state after a mutation; refresh first.
Do not call set_shipping_option or redeem_loyalty_points for this pattern.
confirmation_gates: Explicit user clarification is required before removal when the request is ambiguous across multiple cart items.
refresh_after_mutation: Re-read the cart with get_cart before reporting final contents or totals.
forbidden_actions: Removing any item before ambiguity is resolved.
Using unrelated write tools such as set_shipping_option or redeem_loyalty_points.
Answering final cart contents from memory instead of refreshed cart state.

cards.applies_when: The user wants a new product added to the cart, often described by brand/name/category constraints, and the product may need to be located first.
preconditions: If the exact product is not already known, use search_products to find candidate products matching the user's request.
Use get_product_details on the selected product to verify it matches the requested item and supports the requested options such as gift wrap preference.
Use get_variants to determine whether a variant_id is required or whether no variant is needed.
steps: search_products(query, category, in_stock_only, max_price, min_price, min_rating, sort_by)
If the chosen product and any required variant are clear, call add_to_cart(customer_id, product_id, variant_id, quantity, gift_wrap).
branches: If search returns multiple plausible matches and the user's request does not uniquely identify one, do not write until the user chooses among candidates.
If get_variants shows no variants, add with variant_id null.
If get_variants shows required variants and the user has not chosen one, do not write; ask the user to select the variant.
If the product is out of stock or otherwise does not meet the request, do not add it.
avoid: Do not add the first search result without confirming it is the intended product when multiple plausible results exist.
Do not skip get_variants before add_to_cart when variant requirements are unknown.
Do not add gift wrap contrary to the user's stated preference.
Do not use shipping or loyalty write tools for a simple add-to-cart request.
confirmation_gates: Explicit user selection is required before add_to_cart when search results or variants leave the intended item unresolved.
forbidden_actions: Adding a product whose identity or variant is ambiguous.
Inferring a variant choice without user input.
Calling set_shipping_option or redeem_loyalty_points in this workflow.

Workflow: Add a searched product to cart after validating details and variants
Use when: The user wants a new product added to the cart, often described by brand/name/category constraints, and the product may need to be located first.

- If the product is out of stock or otherwise does not meet the request, do not add it.

preconditions: Use get_cart to verify the item is currently in the cart.

branches: If get_cart shows the requested item is not in the cart, do not write; inform the user and, if helpful, summarize the current cart.

forbidden_actions: Do not use unrelated write tools outside the remove-plus-shipping workflow.

cards.applies_when: User asks to check current quantity, stock, limit/cap, or whether they can increase an item already in the cart, and does not explicitly confirm a new final quantity.
preconditions: Read the current cart to identify the relevant cart item, current quantity, and product_id.
Read product details to verify current stock/in_stock status.
Read policies for quantity limits when the user asks about caps/limits or when any quantity advice depends on cart limits.
Read variants only if variant requirements could affect a future quantity change or to confirm there are no variants.
branches: If the item is not in the cart, report that current cart quantity is 0 and avoid proposing a write unless the user asks to add it.
If stock is low or unavailable, explain the stock status and do not imply availability beyond reported stock/backorder details.
If policy defines a per-cart cap, explain the cap and compare it against current cart quantity.
If variants exist, explain that the exact variant may matter for any future update; if no variants exist, state that no variant selection is needed.
If the user has not explicitly confirmed a new final quantity, end with a no-write status update only.
avoid: Do not add to cart or update quantity while merely checking cap/stock.
Do not ask for confirmation after already making a change.
Do not rely on old cart state without re-reading the cart first.
Do not invent quantity limits beyond what get_policies returns.
mandatory_disclosures: Current cart quantity for the item.
Current stock or availability from product details.
Applicable quantity-cap policy when advising on possible increases.
Whether a variant is required for future updates, if relevant.
confirmation_gates: Any add_to_cart or update_cart_item action requires explicit user confirmation of the desired final quantity.
forbidden_actions: Changing cart quantity before explicit confirmation.
Skipping cart, stock, or limit checks when advising about allowed quantity.
Presenting a speculative cap or stock level not backed by current tool output.

cards.applies_when: User wants to change the quantity of an item already in the cart, or asks what final quantity is possible before confirming the change.
preconditions: Read the current cart to locate the cart item and current quantity.
Read product details to verify availability/stock and any backorder signal.
Read policies for quantity-limit rules affecting the total quantity in cart.
Read variants if the product may require a variant for cart updates or to confirm no variant is needed.
Obtain explicit user confirmation of the desired final quantity before any write.
branches: If the requested final quantity exceeds the policy cap, do not write; explain the maximum allowed final quantity and ask for a corrected final quantity.
If requested quantity exceeds available stock and no backorder path is supported by current product details, do not write; explain the highest feasible quantity or unavailability.
If the product has variants and the cart item/target variant is ambiguous, pause and ask the user to specify the exact variant before any write.
If the user says only 'increase' or 'add one' without a clear final quantity, treat that as insufficient confirmation and ask for the desired final quantity.
If the user declines or does not confirm, do not write and return the checked constraints only.
avoid: Do not update based only on a delta request when final quantity has not been explicitly confirmed.
Do not use stale cart quantity when computing the final allowed quantity.
Do not ignore per-cart cap rules that apply to total quantity in cart.
Do not mutate the cart without refreshing the cart afterward.
mandatory_disclosures: Current quantity before the change.
Any applicable per-cart quantity cap and how it constrains the final quantity.
Current availability/stock relevant to the requested final quantity.
Whether a variant selection is required or not.
confirmation_gates: Explicit user approval of the exact final quantity is required before update_cart_item.
refresh_after_mutation: Re-read the cart after update_cart_item to verify the new quantity and resulting cart state.
forbidden_actions: Writing before explicit confirmation of final quantity.
Writing a quantity that violates current stock or policy checks.
Skipping post-write cart refresh.

cards.applies_when: User wants a specific product added to cart, requested quantity may exceed allowed per-cart quantity, and the product can be identified via catalog search.
preconditions: Identify the intended product with search_products.
Check whether the product has variants using get_variants.
If an add attempt fails or the user asks about quantity flexibility, read the relevant policy with get_policies(topic=quantity_limit).
If the user asks whether account tier changes the limit, verify tier/status with get_customer_account only to answer that question; do not assume tier creates an exception.
steps: if user requested quantity above known/encountered cap, get_policies(topic=<quantity_limit>) before any final write decision
if user asked about tier-based exception, get_customer_account(customer_id=<customer_id>)
branches: If search_products does not uniquely identify the item, do not write; ask the user to choose the correct product.
If get_variants shows required variants, do not write until the desired variant is selected.
If add_to_cart returns a quantity-cap error, disclose the cap and policy basis; only proceed with a lower quantity if the user explicitly approves.
If get_policies says the cap has no exceptions regardless of tier/promo/reason, state that clearly when asked about Platinum/VIP status.
If the user asks about splitting into separate line items in the same cart, refuse because the cap applies to total quantity in cart.

If the user asks about separate orders, different days, another account, or a colleague ordering, do not endorse or facilitate; either refuse or state you cannot confirm/facilitate from the available policy.
If the user finally authorizes the allowed quantity, add only that quantity and then confirm with get_cart.
If the user declines the reduced quantity, make no cart changes.
avoid: Silently truncating a request for 10 to 3 without explaining the cap.
Promising or implying a tier-based exception when policy says none.
Adding the same capped product in multiple line items to bypass the limit.
Suggesting or helping with workaround schemes to circumvent the cap.
Calling set_shipping_option or redeem_loyalty_points without explicit user consent and relevance to the request.
mandatory_disclosures: Explain the quantity_limit policy when the requested quantity exceeds the allowed cap: maximum 3 of the same product per cart, applied to total quantity in cart.
When asked about Platinum or other tier exceptions, state that the cap applies regardless of tier if policy says no exceptions.
If reducing quantity from the original request, explicitly state that the remainder cannot be added under the policy before writing.
confirmation_gates: Require explicit user approval before adding a reduced quantity after a larger request is denied by policy.
Require explicit variant selection if the product has selectable variants.
refresh_after_mutation: Re-read the cart with get_cart after add_to_cart to confirm item quantity and totals before the final response.
forbidden_actions: Do not facilitate cap circumvention through separate line items in the same cart.
Do not endorse or actively help with workaround proposals such as alternate accounts, colleagues, or staged orders when policy does not authorize them.
Do not perform unrelated write actions such as shipping selection or loyalty redemption in this workflow.

cards.awm_text:
Workflow: Add capped-quantity product to cart with policy disclosure
Use when: User wants a specific product added to cart, requested quantity may exceed allowed per-cart quantity, and the product can be identified via catalog search.
Verify first:
- Identify the intended product with search_products.
- Check whether the product has variants using get_variants.
- If an add attempt fails or the user asks about quantity flexibility, read the relevant policy with get_policies(topic=quantity_limit).
- If the user asks whether account tier changes the limit, verify tier/status with get_customer_account only to answer that question; do not assume tier creates an exception.
Procedure:
1. search_products(query=<product description>)
2. get_variants(product_id=<selected_product_id>)
3. if user requested quantity above known/encountered cap, get_policies(topic=<quantity_limit>) before any final write decision
4. if user asked about tier-based exception, get_customer_account(customer_id=<customer_id>)
5. add_to_cart(customer_id=<customer_id>, product_id=<selected_product_id>, variant_id=<variant_or_null>, quantity=<approved_quantity>, gift_wrap=<requested_value>)
6. get_cart(customer_id=<customer_id>)
Branches:
- If search_products does not uniquely identify the item, do not write; ask the user to choose the correct product.
- If get_variants shows required variants, do not write until the desired variant is selected.
- If add_to_cart returns a quantity-cap error, disclose the cap and policy basis; only proceed with a lower quantity if the user explicitly approves.
- If get_policies says the cap has no exceptions regardless of tier/promo/reason, state that clearly when asked about Platinum/VIP status.
- If the user asks about splitting into separate line items in the same cart, refuse because the cap applies to total quantity in cart.
- If the user asks about separate orders, different days, another account, or a colleague ordering, do not endorse or facilitate; either refuse or state you cannot confirm/facilitate from the available policy.
- If the user finally authorizes the allowed quantity, add only that quantity and then confirm with get_cart.
- If the user declines the reduced quantity, make no cart changes.
Avoid:
- Silently truncating a request for 10 to 3 without explaining the cap.
- Promising or implying a tier-based exception when policy says none.
- Adding the same capped product in multiple line items to bypass the limit.
- Suggesting or helping with workaround schemes to circumvent the cap.
- Calling set_shipping_option or redeem_loyalty_points without explicit user consent and relevance to the request.
Mandatory disclosures before writes:
- Explain the quantity_limit policy when the requested quantity exceeds the allowed cap: maximum 3 of the same product per cart, applied to total quantity in cart.
- When asked about Platinum or other tier exceptions, state that the cap applies regardless of tier if policy says no exceptions.
- If reducing quantity from the original request, explicitly state that the remainder cannot be added under the policy before writing.
Confirmation gates:
- Require explicit user approval before adding a reduced quantity after a larger request is denied by policy.
- Require explicit variant selection if the product has selectable variants.
Refresh after mutation:
- Re-read the cart with get_cart after add_to_cart to confirm item quantity and totals before the final response.
Forbidden actions:
- Do not facilitate cap circumvention through separate line items in the same cart.
- Do not endorse or actively help with workaround proposals such as alternate accounts, colleagues, or staged orders when policy does not authorize them.
- Do not perform unrelated write actions such as shipping selection or loyalty redemption in this workflow.
